claim: Prompting an LLM to explicitly measure the gap to the goal, pick an operator for that gap, and recurse on blocked preconditions (MEA, MEDAKA) raises pass@1 on continuous-state planning: Claude-Sonnet-4.6 total 77.8 (CoT) to 94.5, Gemini-3-Flash 65.6 to 82.0, GPT-4o 25.7 to 36.9 (3 rollouts, thinking off). Re-checked against the paper.
agent_test: Add a gap-measure, operator-select, recurse-on-blocked-precondition step to O5; run on a held-out continuous planning set at equal tokens vs CoT.

claim: The MEA gain is not uniform: GPT-5.4 total stays 78.5 (same as AoT+), and on nonlinear problems MEDAKA 46.5 is below AoT+ 49.1. Gains are largest where the CoT baseline is weak. Thinking mode was off for every model, so the paper cannot say whether MEA helps on top of native long reasoning.
agent_test: Test O5 on a strong thinking model; check whether the gap-driven step helps or hurts its native reasoning.

claim: In the MEDAKA ablation, removing state tracking or the recursive module costs 3.5-4.0 points (Claude) and about 6-7 points (Gemini); explicit state tracking is load-bearing. No ablation of operator choice by gap size exists, and no discrete-domain (Blocksworld, Hanoi) test.
agent_test: Ablate explicit state restatement in O5 at equal tokens.

claim: MEDAKA pass@1 beats CoT pass@3 for Claude (94.5 vs 86.8) and Gemini (82.0 vs 67.2), so the gain exceeds simple resampling, except for GPT-5.4 and the Gemma4 models. Caveat: pass@3 is an any-of-3 metric; MEDAKA used 1.8x-3.8x the median tokens of CoT.
agent_test: Compare O5 against CoT best-of-3 at equal total tokens.

claim: Plain CoT or direct prompting on blocks-world planning is poor for non-reasoning LLMs: GPT-4 34.3% on plain Blocksworld (206/600), 4.3% on deceptive Mystery Blocksworld (26/600), 2% randomised; GPT-3 family 1-7%. Human baseline 78% valid plans (39/50).
agent_test: Baseline: run the plain agent on PlanBench-style items to set a floor.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Reasoning models changed the picture: o1-preview solves 97.8% of 3-5 block Blocksworld (587/600) and 52.8% of Mystery Blocksworld, but falls on larger instances and obfuscation; classical Fast Downward is 100% in 0.265 s.
agent_test: Use a classical planner or checker as a reference arm for solvable planning items.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Step-specific CoT helps only when the prompt matches the problem class: GPT-4 table-to-stack 3.83% zero-shot, 59.3% stacking-specific CoT, 51.3% universal-algorithm CoT, 6.89% progression-proof CoT; self-consistency lowered accuracy.
agent_test: Test whether O5 instructions generalise across problem sizes and classes vs tuned exemplars.

claim: Search over reasoning states with an evaluator beats linear CoT on Game of 24 (GPT-4): IO 7.3, CoT 4.0, CoT-SC(100) 9.0, ToT b=1 45, ToT b=5 74. Verified against the paper.
agent_test: Compare O5 with and without branch-and-evaluate at equal tokens. Note the three evidence lines are one paper.

claim: Using an LLM as world model plus planner (RAP, MCTS) lifts Blocksworld success over CoT for 2/4/6-step problems (RAP(10) 1.00/0.86/0.26 vs CoT GPT-4 0.50/0.63/0.40), but 6-step success stays low.
agent_test: Add a one-step lookahead check of the predicted state after each operator.

claim: Subgoal decomposition and as-needed recursion help agents: ADaPT 71.6 vs ReAct 43.3 on ALFWorld; WebShop 44.0 vs 32.0; TextCraft 52.0 vs 19.0; least-to-most 99.7% vs CoT 16.2% on SCAN length split. Re-read of ADaPT: no always-decompose ablation, no token cost reported, single run per model.
agent_test: Recurse only when an action fails (ADaPT-style) vs always decompose, at equal tokens.

claim: A modular planner with subgoal decomposer, monitor and tree search raises Tower of Hanoi 3-disk solve rate from 11% (GPT-4 zero-shot) to 74% (MAP); removing the monitor drops it to 27% with 31% invalid moves; removing the decomposer drops it to 50%.
agent_test: Ablate the monitor (invalid-move check) and decomposer in our loop. All four lines are one paper.

claim: Subgoal-driven frameworks help long-horizon web agents: Gemini-2.5-pro 23.0 to 32.1 percent; stuck-midway errors fall from 48.41 to 39.87 percent.
agent_test: Add a progress check against subgoals to detect stuck states.

claim: Reported collapse of reasoning models on Tower of Hanoi at N>=8 is partly an output-token and evaluation artefact: 15-disk Hanoi needs 32,767 moves at about 10 tokens each; models solve it when asked for a generator function in under 5,000 tokens. Some River Crossing instances (N>=6) were unsolvable. The Lawsen test was preliminary.
agent_test: Ask for programs or compact procedures rather than full move lists when solutions are long.

claim: Even with the algorithm given, collapse stayed near the same N in the Apple study (DeepSeek-R1 at temperature 0 collapsed at N=8); reliable execution of long sequences is a separate weakness from planning.
agent_test: Test whether giving the procedure improves execution at equal tokens; separate planning from execution.

claim: Long procedures need per-step error control: with 1-in-1000 step error a million-step Hanoi fails. MAKER (decomposition, voting k_min=3, red-flag parsing) solved 1,048,575 steps with zero errors using gpt-4.1-mini (per-step error 0.0022, projected $3.5K); haiku-4.5 error 0.184 projects $71.2K; llama-3.2-3B cannot vote. Table values re-checked.
agent_test: Vote on each micro-step for the weakest operator; measure token cost.

claim: Models appear to encode world state internally but fail to use it: probes decode Hanoi state, and steering converts 41% to 73% of optimal solves for Qwen3.6-27B at best strength; R1-Distill-32B fixed 6/72 failures.
agent_test: Not testable on API models; use as motivation for explicit state restatement.

claim: In agentic Hanoi the policy drifts from optimal as n grows, and at n=8 about 40% of the time the model reused previously seen continuations; accuracy drops over 50 points beyond a task threshold on many tasks, while template-friendly Hanoi held longest.
agent_test: Randomise labels (as in Mystery Blocksworld) to separate reasoning from memory.

claim: Obfuscated (Mystery) domains stay much harder than plain ones: GPT-4 34.3% to 4.3% to 2% (deceptive, randomised); o1-preview 97.8% to 52.8% to 37.3%; MAP 27.4% on Mystery.
agent_test: Add renamed-symbol variants to the test set.

claim: In humans, goal-free problems reduce means-ends analysis and improve schema learning versus goal-specific problems (Sweller & Levine 1982, Owen & Sweller 1985, Ayres 1993, Vollmeyer et al. 1996), but the evidence agents did not read these papers, so no effect sizes are available and moderators (strategy use, goal specificity) are unchecked. Gap search: Vollmeyer et al. 1996 abstract (read) says a specific goal pushes difference reduction and less systematic hypothesis testing; systematic rule-induction instruction helped under either goal type, so strategy, not goal-freedom alone, is the mechanism. A 2019 classroom study (N=111) found better far transfer but higher acquisition load for goal-free. Effect sizes and N for the founding studies still unread.
agent_test: No agent test; do not rely on human effect sizes.

claim: Human planning uses subgoals and bottlenecks: with two shortest Hanoi paths people chose the one-bottleneck path in 72% of cases (primary source read: Donnarumma et al. 2016; the subgoaling model also gives 72%); people decompose tasks trading off utility and cost (N=806). No LLM test of a bottleneck rule was found.
agent_test: Choose subgoals at bottlenecks; test bottleneck-aware choice vs nearest-difference.

claim: Pure difference reduction fails on interacting goals (Sussman anomaly): A-on-B then B-on-C undoes the first, and the reverse order also fails. Subgoal order and protecting achieved goals are required.
agent_test: Add a check that a move does not undo achieved subgoals; use Sussman-style items.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: LLM agents largely ignore subgoal interactions; LLM-Modulo with an external verifier back-prompting solved Blocksworld 41/50 (82%), Logistics 35/50 (70%), Mystery 5/50 (10%) within 15 rounds. Gap search: o1-preview on hard Blocksworld rose 23.65% to 98.2% with an external verifier loop (7 iterations, cost $52 to $139 per 100 instances); no study measuring goal ordering or protecting achieved goals was found.
agent_test: Add an external check loop at equal tokens. All lines trace to the Kambhampati group.

claim: Meta-analyses of classroom MEA learning models report large pooled effects (1.431; 0.920 over 18 articles) but are teaching-model studies of unclear quality, not tests of the search heuristic. Gap search: full texts could not be opened; no high-quality study found; recommend dropping both effect sizes.
agent_test: Do not use as evidence for agent design.

claim: GPS founding numbers (task counts, protocol agreement, 16x isomorph difficulty ratios) were recalled, not read, in this run and remain unverified.
agent_test: Fetch Ernst and Newell 1969 and Kotovsky et al. 1985 to confirm.

claim: Transformers trained with chain of computation reach over 99 percent on BlocksWorld and Pancake and solve Hanoi up to 20 disks, so failures are about missing procedure, not architecture limits.
agent_test: Training; out of scope for a scaffold.

claim: At equal inference compute, majority-vote self-consistency beats LLM generative verification at most budgets: GenRM matches SC only at about 8x SC compute (Llama-3.1-8B, MATH) and beats it at about 128x (+3.8%). An exact external checker is different: o1-preview hard Blocksworld 23.65% to 98.2% with a verifier loop at about 2.7x cost.
agent_test: Compare, at equal tokens, (a) more samples with vote, (b) soft self-check per step, (c) exact rule check per step, on a held-out planning set.

claim: Structured or step-by-step prompting adds little on top of native long reasoning: on GPQA Diamond (4,950 runs per prompt per model) CoT gave o3-mini +2.9, o4-mini +3.1, Gemini Flash 2.5 -3.3 points, with 20-80% more time; thinking vs non-thinking at matched tokens shows non-thinking as good or better at low complexity.
agent_test: Run the gap-driven O5 with thinking on and off at equal tokens on a held-out planning set; keep it only where it wins.

claim: Only recursion and state tracking of MEDAKA were ablated (each worth 3.5-7 points, mostly on nonlinear, coupling, multi-goal tags); choosing operators by gap size was never ablated and transfer to discrete domains (Blocksworld, Hanoi, code) was never tested.
agent_test: Ablate operator choice by gap size on a discrete domain with a validator.

claim: Having the model write operator (successor and goal-test) code once and running ordinary search solved 24 Game, crosswords, BlocksWorld (4-5 blocks) and PrOntoQA at 100% with about 2-4 model calls, against projected 200K-560K calls for tree-search methods on BlocksWorld.
agent_test: Test code-defined operators with an exact checker against per-step LLM operator choice on Blocksworld at equal tokens.

claim: Renamed or counterfactual variants lower plain-model results: GPT-4 Blocksworld 34.3% to 4.3% (deceptive) and 2% (randomized); GPT-3.5 program parse rate 99% to 62-75% under counterfactual rules. Default and counterfactual scores are correlated, so success is a mix of recall and transferable reasoning. No scaffold-vs-plain comparison on renamed Hanoi was found.
agent_test: Run every O5 test on a symbol-renamed twin of the task.
